learning_objective: 🎯 Learn how the government plans its finances for the year, taxes its citizens, and spends money to keep the economy stable and growing.

main_concepts.simple_explanation: It's an annual financial statement showing the government's estimated receipts (income) and estimated expenditure (spending) for the upcoming fiscal year.

Revenue receipts neither create a liability nor reduce assets (e.g., Taxes). Capital receipts either create a liability (e.g., Borrowing money) or reduce an asset (e.g., Selling government shares/Disinvestment).

Revenue expenditure doesn't create assets or reduce liabilities (e.g., Paying salaries, pensions). Capital expenditure creates assets (e.g., Building roads) or reduces liabilities (e.g., Repaying a loan).
Revenue Deficit = Revenue Expenditure - Revenue Receipts. Fiscal Deficit = Total Expenditure - Total Receipts (excluding borrowings). Primary Deficit = Fiscal Deficit - Interest Payments.

fun_activity.title: 🧾 You are the Finance Minister
fun_activity.instructions: Your country is facing high inflation. You need to cool down the economy. Do you increase or decrease taxes? Answer: You INCREASE taxes! This leaves people with less disposable income, which lowers aggregate demand and helps bring prices down.

exam_tips: 📌 A classic board question: Classify given items into Revenue or Capital receipts/expenditure. Always use the 'Asset/Liability' test to decide.
📌 Fiscal Deficit is exactly equal to the total borrowing requirements of the government.
📌 Understand the difference between Direct Taxes (Income Tax, paid directly) and Indirect Taxes (GST, burden can be shifted to others).
quick_recap: ⭐ The budget helps the government reallocate resources, reduce inequalities, and stabilize the economy.
⭐ Primary deficit shows the borrowing requirements of the government strictly for current expenses, ignoring past debts (interest).
⭐ A zero primary deficit means the government is only borrowing to pay interest on past loans.
